legend: Macroscopic appearance of a malignant AME shows a poorly defined lobulated tumour with a greyish-beige fleshy surface, with focal haemorrhage and yellowish foci of necrosis.
Low magnification shows a papillary tumour with a biphasic appearance of both epithelial and prominent myoepithelial cells, indicating a papillary AME.
Higher magnification shows classic AME with epithelial tubules immersed among sheets of myoepithelial cells.
Invasive carcinoma comprising narrow trabeculae and irregular tumour nests are seen at the periphery of the AME.

Invasive carcinoma shows spindled abnormal myoepithelial cells with nuclear atypia and mitotic activity, regarded as metaplastic spindle cell carcinoma (another area of the same tumour is illustrated in Fig. <<#51335>>).
The invasive carcinoma also shows squamous differentiation as part of the metaplastic carcinoma (another area of the same tumour is illustrated in Fig. <<#51334>>).
CK7 is strongly expressed by epithelial tubules within the adenomyoepithelioma on immunohistochemistry, while the myoepithelial cells are faintly highlighted.
CK14 decorates the invasive carcinoma that extends from the periphery of the adenomyoepithelioma into the surrounding breast tissue.
Mastectomy specimen shows a large lobulated poorly defined tumour abutting the breast skin.

Malignant adenomyoepithelioma with a biphasic proliferation of epithelial and myoepithelial cells and areas displaying papillary architecture. Necrosis, haemorrhage and skin erosion are present. Nuclear atypia is seen in both epithelial and myoepithelial components. Mitoses number up to 9 per 10 high power fields, field diameter 0.6mm.

diagnosis: Epithelial myoepithelial neoplasm, with features of adenomyoepithelioma with malignant transformation in myoepithelial component (metaplastic type carcinoma, SBR grade 2)
legend:
Malignant adenomyoepithelioma with metaplastic carcinoma 
Adenomyoepithelioma shows a biphasic epithelial-myoepithelial proliferation in a papillary architecture, with the myoepithelial component transitioning into metaplastic carcinoma with spindle and squamous components.
